title: How can every digit be written with a power of ten?
description: A place chart splits five thousand six hundred forty two into thousands, hundreds, tens and ones, and each place becomes a digit times a power of ten. The chart then runs past the point, where tenths, hundredths and thousandths take negative exponents. Keeko doubts that the nine in the decimal is nine times ten to the power one.
teaching_notes: One idea: every place is a power of ten, and the places after the decimal point use negative exponents. Watch for students who give the tenths place the exponent one.

source: Write 5642 in expanded form with powers of 10, and write 561
video_script.why: The child knows place value, and now joins it to powers of ten, including the negative exponents after the point.
video_script.substitution: Read each digit's place, write the place as a power of ten, and multiply it by the digit.
video_script.anchor: the numbers 5642 and 561.903 on a place chart
video_script.wrong_answer: nine times ten to the power one
video_script.wrong_move: Keeko gives the tenths place the exponent one, so the nine becomes ninety. Places after the point get smaller by ten each time, so they take negative exponents.
video_script.payoff_line: Every digit is multiplied by the power of ten for its place

final_answer.spoken: the tenths are nine times ten to the power minus one, the hundredths zero times ten to the power minus two, and the thousandths three times ten to the power minus three

maths_rules: the slip: 9 × 10¹ = 90, but the 9 after the point is nine tenths
video_script.design: One place chart stays on the stage for the whole video. It grows to the right of the point in the fourth step. The two numbers sit in the working area, one line per step.

<bookmark mark='num'/>It gives the number five thousand six hundred forty two.

narration: <bookmark mark='chart'/>Here is a place chart with thousands, hundreds, tens and ones.
<bookmark mark='ten'/>Each place is ten times the place on its right.
<bookmark mark='pow'/>Thousands are ten cubed and hundreds are ten squared.
Tens are ten to the power one, and ones are ten to the power zero.

narration: <bookmark mark='given'/>Given, the first number is five thousand six hundred forty two.
<bookmark mark='dec'/>The second is five hundred sixty one point nine zero three.

narration: <bookmark mark='find'/>We have to write each number with powers of ten.

beats.colours: each place in its own colour
narration: <bookmark mark='split'/>Step one, split five thousand six hundred forty two by place value.
<bookmark mark='parts'/>It is five thousands, six hundreds, four tens and two ones.

marks.mult: each digit is joined to the power of ten of its place

beats.colours: digits in one colour, powers of ten in another
narration: <bookmark mark='mult'/>Step two, multiply each digit by the power of ten for its place.
<bookmark mark='write'/>Five times ten cubed, plus six times ten squared.
Then four times ten to the power one, plus two times ten to the power zero.
<bookmark mark='check'/>Adding the parts back gives the number again.

marks.dec2: the chart extends to the right of the point with tenths, hundredths and thousandths

narration: <bookmark mark='split2'/>Step three, split the second number by place value.
It is five hundreds, six tens, and one in the ones place.
<bookmark mark='dec2'/>Then nine tenths, no hundredths, and three thousandths.

narration: <bookmark mark='neg'/>Step four, find the powers for the places after the point.
Each place is ten times smaller than the one before it.
<bookmark mark='exp'/>Tenths, hundredths and thousandths are ten to the power minus one, minus two and minus three.

marks.ans: the full line is written and boxed

beats.colours: digits in one colour, powers of ten in another
narration: <bookmark mark='ans'/>Every digit is multiplied by the power of ten for its place.
<bookmark mark='tenth'/>In the second number, the tenths are nine times ten to the power minus one.
The hundredths are zero times ten to the power minus two.
<bookmark mark='thou'/>The thousandths are three times ten to the power minus three.

narration: <bookmark mark='hand'/>Keeko has raised a hand. Let us check the doubt and solve it.

marks.doubt: the bubble 9 × 10¹ appears beside the nine
marks.ninety: the bubble changes to 90 and is crossed out

beats.colours: the wrong bubble in the warning colour
narration: <bookmark mark='doubt'/>Keeko thinks the nine after the point is nine times ten to the power one.
<bookmark mark='ninety'/>But ten to the power one is ten, and nine times ten is ninety.
<bookmark mark='fix'/>The nine is only nine tenths, a small part of one.
That needs ten to the power minus one.
